taxonomy.subtopic: Loss of inhibitory myenteric neurons and failure of lower esophageal sphincter relaxation

questions.stem_html: A 39-year-old woman has 8 months of progressive difficulty swallowing both liquids and solids, nocturnal regurgitation of undigested food, and a 5-kg weight loss. Endoscopy shows no obstructing lesion. The accompanying manometry schematic shows absent propagated contractions in the distal esophagus and incomplete relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter after a swallow. Which cellular change most directly produces this pattern?

options.text_html: Selective loss of nitric oxide- and vasoactive intestinal peptide-releasing neurons in the myenteric plexus
Selective destruction of excitatory cholinergic neurons that contract esophageal smooth muscle
Hyperplasia of gastrin-secreting cells with excessive gastric acid production
Loss of secretomotor neurons in the submucosal plexus of the esophagus
Degeneration of somatic vagal fibers supplying the proximal striated esophagus

questions.explanation_html: Normal swallowing activates inhibitory myenteric neurons that release nitric oxide and vasoactive intestinal peptide, relaxing the distal esophageal smooth muscle and lower esophageal sphincter ahead of the bolus. Achalasia preferentially destroys these inhibitory neurons while excitatory cholinergic activity is relatively preserved. The resulting unopposed excitation causes impaired sphincter relaxation, functional outflow obstruction, and loss of coordinated peristalsis.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Loss of excitatory cholinergic neurons would reduce contractile tone rather than create a hypertensive, nonrelaxing sphincter.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Excess gastrin can increase acid secretion but does not explain aperistalsis and incomplete swallow-induced sphincter relaxation.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: The submucosal plexus primarily regulates secretion and local blood flow; the characteristic motor defect arises in the myenteric plexus.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Somatic vagal fibers control proximal striated muscle and do not account for the distal smooth-muscle and sphincter pattern.

questions.educational_objective: Achalasia results from loss of inhibitory nitric oxide/VIP myenteric neurons, causing absent distal peristalsis and impaired lower esophageal sphincter relaxation.
